summary: ContentId for attachments does not surround the CID with less/greater thans.

comments.content:
The sample below shows that the Content-ID header does not surround the
value with less/greater thans.

    ------=_Part_5_32099189.1270971890145
    Content-Type: image/test;
filename=cid:attachment%2d1;name=cid:attachment%2d1
    Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
    Content-Disposition: inline; size=0; filename="cid:attachment%2d1"
    Content-ID: cid:attachment%2d1

I cannot comment if this is a rquirement/mandatory but according to the RFC
http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2387.txt and then jump to page 5 and scan for
section 5.2. It gives the following sample which does include less/greater
thans around a ContentId value. 

 {/doc}
     --example-2
     Content-Type: image/jpeg
     Content-ID: <950118.AFDH@XIson.com>
     Content-Transfer-Encoding: BASE64
     Content-Description: Picture A

     [encoded jpeg image]
     --example-2
     Content-Type: image/jpeg
     Content-ID: <950118.AECB@XIson.com>
     Content-Transfer-Encoding: BASE64
     Content-Description: Picture B

In the spirit of correctness it would seem to be a good idea to fix this.

The fix, though i have not confired it but it makes sense this is the right
spot is quite simple.
Class:  Mailer
method: getBodyPartFromDatasource
Line:   attachmentPart.setHeader("Content-ID", ds.getName());
Fixed:  attachmentPart.setHeader("Content-ID", "<" + ds.getName()+ ">");

Excellent. I'll see if I can get it in by the weekend. I might provide a branch 
release for this temporarily, since I'm unable to comprehensively test the change.

I've checked in this fix, but won't update the jars just yet. Please test the update 
using the latest source code (from the trunk).
